name: Labrador Retriever
grooming: Moderate; regular brushing, heavier seasonal shedding
temperament: Friendly, outgoing, active, and eager to please
pros: Usually sociable and people-oriented
Often trainable and enthusiastic about activities
Can be a versatile family and sporting companion
cons: Needs substantial daily exercise and mental stimulation
Sheds year-round, with heavier seasonal shedding
Can become boisterous or destructive when under-exercised

name: Golden Retriever
grooming: Moderate to high; regular brushing and seasonal shedding
temperament: Friendly, intelligent, devoted, and eager to please
pros: Often affectionate and social
Typically responsive to reward-based training
Enjoys outdoor activities and family participation
cons: Needs daily exercise and companionship
Sheds noticeably, especially seasonally
Long coat needs regular brushing and care

name: German Shepherd Dog
grooming: Moderate; frequent brushing and substantial shedding
pros: Highly trainable when consistently handled
Often excels in dog sports and working roles
Loyal and attentive to its household
cons: Requires consistent training, socialization, and exercise
Can be reserved with strangers
Sheds heavily and needs regular coat care

name: French Bulldog
grooming: Low; occasional brushing and routine skin-fold care
pros: Usually adapts well to smaller living spaces
Generally enjoys close human companionship
Typically does not require intense exercise
cons: Flat-faced structure can cause serious breathing and heat-tolerance problems
May have significant veterinary-care needs
Not suited to strenuous exercise or hot weather

name: Poodle (Standard)
grooming: High; frequent professional or careful home coat maintenance
pros: Very intelligent and often quick to learn
Low-shedding coat may suit some allergy-conscious homes (no dog is truly hypoallergenic)
Enjoys training, games, and many dog sports
cons: Coat requires significant ongoing grooming
Needs daily physical and mental activity
Can become bored without engagement

name: Beagle
grooming: Low; regular brushing and basic ear care
pros: Often cheerful and sociable
Manageable coat-care needs
Enjoys walks, scent games, and exploring
cons: Strong scent drive can make off-leash reliability difficult
May bark, bay, or howl
Needs secure containment and patient training

name: Bulldog
grooming: Low to moderate; routine skin-fold cleaning
pros: Often enjoys a relaxed home routine
Usually does not need intense exercise
Distinctive, affectionate companion for many households
cons: Flat-faced anatomy can affect breathing and heat tolerance
Skin folds need regular cleaning and drying
May have substantial health-care needs

name: Dachshund
grooming: Varies by coat; smooth is low, longhaired needs more brushing
pros: Small size can suit many homes
Playful and often strongly bonded to family
Comes in three coat varieties
cons: Long back makes weight control and avoiding repeated jumping important
Can be vocal and independent
May follow scents and ignore recall

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
grooming: Moderate; regular brushing and shedding management
pros: Intelligent and often enjoys learning
Compact but sturdy
Can be an engaging companion for active households
cons: Needs exercise and mental work
Can bark and may try to herd people or other pets
Sheds considerably and needs weight management

name: Australian Shepherd
grooming: Moderate; regular brushing and seasonal shedding
pros: Excels at training and canine sports
Often forms close bonds with its people
A strong match for active owners who enjoy teaching skills
cons: Needs substantial daily exercise and mental challenges
May attempt to herd children, pets, or moving objects
Can become anxious or destructive when under-stimulated

name: Boxer
pros: Often playful and affectionate
Short coat is relatively easy to maintain
Enjoys active games and family participation
cons: Can be exuberant and needs training
Needs regular exercise and attention
Flat-faced features may affect heat tolerance and breathing

name: Shih Tzu
grooming: High; daily brushing for a long coat or regular trims
pros: Often content with indoor companionship
Small size suits many living arrangements
Usually enjoys being with people
cons: Long coat requires frequent grooming
Can be difficult to house-train without consistency
Short muzzle can contribute to breathing and heat issues
